title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Tuscany and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show the DOCG, like Chianti Classico, Brunello di Montalcino or Vino Nobile, or Toscana IGT for Super Tuscans, plus producer, vintage and sometimes Riserva, Gran Selezione or a UGA. The pink DOCG neck strip and, for Chianti Classico, the black rooster confirm origin.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Sangiovese's acidity loves tomato and olive oil: pasta with tomato sauce, pappardelle with wild boar ragù, ribollita, a bread and bean soup, and bistecca alla fiorentina, a thick grilled T-bone. Brunello suits game and aged pecorino. Vernaccia and Vermentino suit seafood. Vin Santo suits cantucci.

steps.prompt: Which dish is a Tuscan classic with Chianti Classico or Brunello?

steps.title: Service
steps.body: Serve Tuscan reds at 16 to 18 degrees. Chianti Classico Annata is best within five years; Riserva and Gran Selezione 10 to 20; Brunello 15 to 30. Decant young Brunello and Super Tuscans.

steps.explanation: Chocolate mousse needs a sweet wine.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show DOCG or IGT, with Riserva or Gran Selezione
Sangiovese suits tomato, boar and bistecca
